Where did the flight lose time?

The departure operations team compares the same flight number across several dates. Analysing ground preparation requires distinguishing flight-level boarding closure from scans of individual bags.

The operations request

I want to compare departure preparation for on-time and delayed flights. For each outbound flight, show when boarding started and closed, when baggage loading closed, when the aircraft was ready, and when it actually went off-block. List the events in chronological order.

Each case is a dated outbound operating leg. Scheduled departure is a flight attribute, and the trace contains actual events.

FlightScheduled off-blockBoarding startBoarding closeBaggage loading closeAircraft readyActual off-block
F001 · AX10109:0008:2008:4808:5108:5609:00
F005 · AX10109:0008:2008:4909:1309:1909:25

In the 1–2 December example, boarding closure differs by one minute, baggage loading closure by 22 minutes, and actual off-block by 25 minutes. These differences identify intervals for further investigation.

From database records to an event log

StepDecision in this example
EEG constructionIn handling_jobs, BL identifies flight-level baggage loading closure. finished_at records actual completion, and posted_at records system posting. Follow turn_id to the turnaround and outbound_id to the operating leg.
Request interpretationChoose the outbound flight as the case and select the five activities named in the request. Individual LD bag scans and passenger-level boarding confirmations are outside this request.
Specification and compilationProject finished_at from each BL row and the associated flight ID. Combine the activity-specific results with UNION ALL.
VerificationRun the reference SQL and compare its output with the authored reference log, preserving event multiplicities. Model extraction is evaluated separately.

From inbound arrival to the next take-off

Request T uses a turnaround as the case. U001 links inbound flight I001 to outbound flight F001. Dispatch records in the 20-table database confirm that both legs use the same aircraft. The example below is from 1 December.

caseActivityActual event time
U001Inbound landed2026-12-01 07:20:00
U001Inbound in-block2026-12-01 07:30:00
U001Ground handling started2026-12-01 07:32:00
U001Disembarkation completed2026-12-01 07:41:00
U001Baggage unloading completed2026-12-01 07:46:00
U001Cabin cleaning completed2026-12-01 08:10:00
U001Refuelling completed2026-12-01 08:12:00
U001Catering completed2026-12-01 08:15:00
U001Boarding start2026-12-01 08:20:00
U001Boarding close2026-12-01 08:48:00

U001Off-block2026-12-01 09:00:00

The trace distinguishes taxi-in (landing to in-block), turnaround (in-block to off-block), and taxi-out (off-block to take-off). Handling tasks can overlap. Chronological order records observed timing. The example simplifies clearances, de-icing and aircraft swaps.

Extraction requests

IDMinimum tablesRequestCasesReference events
T5I want to compare aircraft turnarounds from an inbound arrival to the next departure. For each turnaround, show the inbound flight's landing and in-block arrival, the start of ground handling, completion of passenger disembarkation, baggage unloading, cabin cleaning, refuelling and catering loading, then the outbound flight's boarding start and close, baggage loading close, aircraft ready time, off-block departure and take-off. List the events in chronological order.48672
D5I want to compare departure preparation for on-time and delayed flights. For each outbound flight, show when boarding started and closed, when baggage loading closed, when the aircraft was ready, and when it actually went off-block. List the events in chronological order.48240
P10For each passenger flight leg, show the records for completed check-in and confirmed boarding at the gate.288576
S15I want to analyse security queue time and screening time separately. For each security checkpoint visit, show when the passenger joined the queue, when screening began and when it finished, in chronological order.288864
B15For each passenger flight leg, show completed check-in and confirmed boarding. If the passenger checked any bags, also show when each bag was accepted and loaded.288864

Security queue time is screening start minus queue entry. Screening duration is completion minus screening start. For prediction, use only information available at prediction time.

Sources and assumptions

This synthetic research schema draws on public descriptions of bookings, tickets, operating legs, ground preparation and baggage handling. It assumes access to linked airport screening and handling records. All timestamps are in KST.

  • EUROCONTROL A-CDM Specification
  • Postgres Pro Airlines schema
  • IATA baggage tracking guide

Movement reports include source, validation method and message format. Handling jobs include service provider, dispatch priority and work zone. The attributes are synthetic and informed by IATA AIDX and EUROCONTROL A-CDM. The kind and job_code columns still identify activities.

Passenger attributes and public models

The passengers table stores synthetic dates of birth, nationality codes and gender codes. Date of birth is a passenger attribute. The dataset records a single nationality, distinct from country of residence or document issuance. The local gender codes are MALE, FEMALE and UNKNOWN.

Public sourceHow the source informed the dataset
Postgres Pro Airlines (2017 schema family)This demo database defines bookings, tickets and ticket_flights. The demo stores passenger data in tickets. AirlineFlow uses a separate passengers table with internal synthetic passenger IDs.
Amadeus booking exampleThe booking API example places dateOfBirth and gender on the traveller and nationality on the travel document. AirlineFlow stores nationality on the passenger record.
EUROCONTROL A-CDMA-CDM informs the distinction between boarding, aircraft readiness and departure. The inbound_id and outbound_id fields link legs operated by the same aircraft. Request T combines inbound LAND and IN, ground handling, and outbound OUT and AIR. The example uses completed turnarounds with no aircraft swaps.

The dataset simplifies fares, payments, seats, travel document history, rebooking, diversions and repeated boarding sessions. Each flight contains a sample of passenger and baggage records. Flight-level closure times come from dedicated handling records.
